faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: A web app you install from the browser, without going through a store. It opens full-screen from its icon, like a regular app, and updates itself.
faq.q2: How do I install Lien Parental on my phone?
faq.a2: Open the site in your browser, then choose “Add to Home Screen” (share menu on iPhone, browser menu on Android). Our Install the app page guides you step by step.
faq.q3: Is the Parenting guide available everywhere?
faq.a3: Not yet. The Guide starts with French Guiana, with sheets on school, health, benefits, separation and daily life, then opens up territory by territory: Martinique, Guadeloupe, Réunion, Mayotte and mainland France. The Parenting guide page shows which territories are already available.
faq.a4: Yes. Exchanges are encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and data is encrypted at rest. Your data is stored in the European Union (Ireland); some providers (payment, email, AI Coach) may process part of it outside the EU, with the safeguards required by the GDPR (details in the privacy policy). Health data has additional encryption. Your space is personal: nothing is shared without your consent.
faq.q5: Can I share information with the other parent?
faq.a5: Yes, with “Linked parents”. You invite the other parent and choose what you share for each child: profile, calendar, documents or expenses. Your Journal, the AI Coach and your unshared documents stay private.
faq.q6: Can I cancel my subscription at any time?
faq.a6: Yes. Paid plans have no commitment and can be cancelled from your profile. You keep access until the end of the paid period, then your data stays viewable on the free plan.

about.title: Lien Parental, protecting the parent-child bond
about.lead: Lien Parental is an app for separated parents: organize the child’s daily life, communicate calmly, keep important documents and understand administrative procedures.
about.whoBody: Lien Parental is a service published by Pirabel Labs. Full legal information (publisher, hosting provider, director of publication) is available in the legal notice.
about.whereBody: The Parenting guide is designed first for “{territory}”, with {count, plural, one {# fact sheet} other {# fact sheets}} and step-by-step paths. The app itself works everywhere, on the web and as an app installed on your phone.
about.for1: Separated parents, or parents going through a separation, who organize their child’s life between two homes.
about.for2: Families looking for reliable information about their procedures: health, school, benefits, family justice.
about.for3: Parents who need to keep a clear, dated record of exchanges and documents.
about.methodTitle: How we check the guide’s fact sheets
about.method1: Each fact sheet cites its official sources (Service-Public.fr, Caf, local administrations and organizations), with a link to each one.
about.method2: Each fact sheet shows the date it was last checked. The most recent review is dated {date}.
about.method3: Before publication, each fact sheet is checked automatically: complete structure, sources present, valid links between fact sheets and paths.
about.method4: Local information we could not confirm is never presented as established fact.
about.legalBody: Lien Parental informs and helps you get organized, but it does not replace a lawyer or personalized legal advice. For a specific situation, contact a lawyer, a family mediator or a free legal advice point (point-justice).
about.dataBody: Data is hosted in the European Union and encrypted in transit and at rest. Details are available in the <link>privacy policy</link>.
